.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r1/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md section 2 (Verify: sentence variety, contractions, occasional terse fragment; Defect: uniform cadence, marketing gloss, perfectly parallel bullets, voice change between instruction.md and notes)
evidence: instruction.md reads as a first-person team lead talking: opens with a question ('Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' instruction.md:1), states the hard part plainly ('the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' :1), uses I/we/our throughout ('I want that to work without dragging as well as with it' :3; 'tell me who' :3; 'I often move several candidates together' :3), contractions (nobody's :1, people's :5, don't :11/:13, it's :13, mustn't :13), varied sentence length including short ones ('Candidates sign in too.' :9; 'Interview has a limited number of places per job.' :3; 'layout and names are yours.' :11; 'A clear desktop workspace is what matters.' :11), and no bullets, headings or numbered lists. Grep for marketing/LLM gloss (seamless|robust|delve|leverage|ensure|comprehensive|intuitive|streamlin) over instruction.md and both notes returned zero hits. hireops_rules.md is a reference rules note and is appropriately more structured (tables, bullets), but keeps the same owner voice: 'These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace. Follow them exactly.' (:3), 'what we care about is that the workspace behaves the way this note says' (:4-5), 'What it's for' (:14), 'Where drafts are kept is yours.' (:175), 'between our side and the candidate' (:127). Bullets are role/rule enumerations whose parallelism is content-driven (e.g. §6 'Who takes part' :131-134), not decorative. integration.md is almost verbatim the template's frozen integration.md plus one task-added delivery paragraph (:16-19), so its impersonal tone is template-controlled, not an authoring voice defect. Minor observations, not defects: (a) spelling register drifts: instruction.md uses British 'honour'/'honouring' (:13) while hireops_rules.md:200 uses 'Honor' and template integration.md:7 'honoring'; (b) hireops_rules.md §8 'Runtime file paths' (:197-201) shifts into an impersonal runtime-contract register ('Resolve bundled UI and seed files relative to the entry or module directory'), which reads as harness boilerplate; (c) instruction.md:13 is a dense one-sentence runtime list ('It must start with ..., listen on ..., expose ..., serve ..., and keep ...') - a slightly spec-like run but still conversational ('How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call', 'so don't install packages'). (d) hireops_rules.md lines 99, 112 and 173 contain overlong spliced lines inside otherwise wrapped paragraphs (editing seam, not voice; relevant to row 3 rather than this row). None of these makes the prose robotic, over-polished or LLM-sounding; the check's 'casual/terse is good' bar is met. Counterexample attempt: a hypothetical reviewer arguing the rules note is a 'shall/must spec' - refuted for this row because the workbook targets voice, and the note keeps first-person-plural owner phrasing and terse fragments; spec-structure concerns belong to row 1, which scores instruction.md, not the reference note. App-level broken/conforming alternatives are not applicable: this row grades prose, not app behavior; no runtime evidence is required.
suggested_fix: Optional polish only (P3, not required): align spelling register (e.g. 'Honour' at hireops_rules.md:200 to match instruction.md:13, leaving template integration.md untouched) and rewrap the spliced long lines at hireops_rules.md:99/112/173.
